en.html:
Muramasa"A bridge?"
Kageaki"What remains of one."

ja.html:
村正「橋？」
景明「の、名残りだな」
ja.text: 村正「橋？」景明「の、名残りだな」

en.html:
I stood beside a river, not very wide but apparently deep, and checked the facts.

A rough but useful wooden bridge must once have crossed it. Now the remains of the framework sat on both banks, contributing nothing.

Last night, when I stepped into that argument... I could not remember the details, but I had certainly heard 'bridge' several times. Someone had broken the bridge, or something like that.

This had to be the one. It seemed this bridge was the reason those people had been arguing with their hostility fully on display.

ja.html:
幅は然程でもないが、深さがありそうな川のほとり。
　そこに立って、事実を確認する。

　粗末ながら有用な木橋が、嘗てここに架かっていた
のだろう。
　今は何の役にも立たない木組が両岸に残るばかりだ
が。

　昨晩、言い合いの中に分け入った時……詳細は思い
出せないが、確かに橋という単語を何度も聴いた。
　橋を壊したとか、どうとか。

　これの事に違いない。
　この橋が原因で、昨夜の人々は敵意も露わに争って
いた様子だった。

I turned toward the voices. Two men, apparently local residents. Their work clothes suggested they were on their way to work.

I did not recognize them. They seemed to recognize me.

...Then were they part of last night's argument?

Leaving Muramasa where she was, I went over to them.

en.html:
One of the men had quite a carrying voice. Neighbors were starting to look over: women doing the washing, a young man just out of bed.

Few of those looks were disapproving. Most seemed to agree.

A sudden increase in population, worse living conditions, and the established residents full of resentment. Was that the situation? If the public authorities had anything to spare, one might expect proper measures. At present, that was not a hope available to us.

This problem was not a small one.

ja.html:
男性の一方は、声がかなり大きい。
　洗濯中の主婦や、置き抜けの青年など、周辺の住民
から視線を集めつつあった。

　しかしその中に、非難の色は薄い。
　賛同の意思を寄せるものが大半だった。

　人口の急増で生活環境が悪化したため、旧来の住民
はみな強い不満を抱いている……そういう事か。
　公的機関に余力があれば適切な措置も期待できるが、
今は望むべくもない。

　これは中々、厄介な問題のようだ。

en.html:
Kageaki"About this bridge, then."
Resident A"Ah... that is their doing as well."
Resident A"We used it to get into town. Now that it's broken, everyone with a workplace on the other side has to go far downstream and cross another bridge."
Resident A"Do you know how much extra walking that is?"
Resident B"Ridiculous business..."
Kageaki"The refugees broke it?"
Resident B"Does that look like damage from wind or a flood?"
Kageaki"No. But what evidence is there that the refugees did it?"
Resident A"Evidence... none. But who else would?"
Resident A"They live across the river too. We keep going over to complain, and they don't like it. So they broke the bridge. Must be that."
Resident B"I don't say every one of them is stupid enough to think no bridge means no complaints. But it was an old bridge. One such idiot would be enough to bring it down easily."
Kageaki"..."
Resident A"Do something about it, officer."
Kageaki"Yes. I would like to establish the facts and take appropriate action."
Resident B"'Appropriate action.' An official's appropriate action, that is a difficult thing to depend on."
Resident A"Should we ask the underworld fellows after all?"
Resident B"The ones who said they'd patrol around here?"
Resident A"Not just patrol. They said we could discuss getting the refugees driven out, too."
Resident B"But you heard the protection fee, no? Where will that much money come from every month?"
Resident A"That is the trouble... Those fellows know how badly we need help, and they're charging accordingly."

ja.html:
景明「ところで、この橋ですが」
住民Ａ「あぁ…… 　そいつも、奴らのせいさ」
住民Ａ「街中へ行くのに使う橋だってのに。 　これを壊されちまったせいで、あっち側に 仕事場のある奴はみんな、ずっと下流の別の 橋を渡っていかなきゃならなくなった」
住民Ａ「すげえ遠回りなんだぜ？」
住民Ｂ「馬鹿馬鹿しいよな……」
景明「難民の人々がこれを壊したのですか？」
住民Ｂ「風や増水で壊れたようには見えないだろ？」
景明「確かに。 　しかし、難民の犯行という証拠は？」
住民Ａ「証拠は……ねえさ。 　けどよ、他に誰がやるってんだ」
住民Ａ「あいつら、俺達がちょくちょく苦情を言い に行くのが嫌で、橋を壊したに決まってる。 　難民どもが住んでるのも川向こうだからな」
住民Ｂ「あいつら全員が、橋さえ無ければ文句言わ れないなんて考える馬鹿だとは思わねえけど。 　古い橋だったからな。そういう馬鹿が一人 でもいれば、簡単に落とせるんだ」
景明「…………」
住民Ａ「お巡り、どうにかしてくれよ」
景明「そうですね。 　事態を確かめ、善処したく思います」
住民Ｂ「善処ね。 　お役人の善処はアテにならないからなぁ」
住民Ａ「やっぱり、筋・の連中に頼むか？」
住民Ｂ「この辺りの見回りを請け負ってくれるって 話か」
住民Ａ「それだけじゃねえ。 　難民どもの追い出しも、相談に乗るってさ」
住民Ｂ「でもよ、みかじめ料を聞いただろ？ 　どうやって毎月、それだけの金を出すんだ」
住民Ａ「そこがな……。 　あいつら、こっちの足元を見てやがるから」
